issue.title: Support init scripts for `MongoDBContainer` without manually customizing the `WaitStrategy`

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

issue.body:
A container initialized as follows, fails to start:
```		
MongoDBContainer c = new MongoDBContainer(MONGO_IMAGE)
		.withEnv("MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME", "root")
		.withEnv("MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD", "password" )
		.withFileSystemBind("init/mongo-init.js",
			"/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/mongo-init.js", BindMode.READ_ONLY)
		;
		c.start()
```
Not sure but probably because the docker-entrypoint.sh, in case of presence of init-db scripts, does a shutdown and a restart of the process after executing them:
```
if [ -n "$shouldPerformInitdb" ]; then
...
		echo
		for f in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/*; do
			case "$f" in
				*.sh) echo "$0: running $f"; . "$f" ;;
				*.js) echo "$0: running $f"; "${mongo[@]}" "$MONGO_INITDB_DATABASE" "$f"; echo ;;
				*)    echo "$0: ignoring $f" ;;
			esac
			echo
		done

		"${mongodHackedArgs[@]}" --shutdown
		rm -f "$pidfile"
...
```

body:
@vcvitaly is correct, this is about the change in the log format (which we actually already briefly discussed in Slack).

> Starting in MongoDB 4.4, mongod / mongos instances now output all log messages in structured JSON format. Log entries are written as a series of key-value pairs, where each key indicates a log message field type, such as “severity”, and each corresponding value records the associated logging information for that field type, such as “informational”.

Besides from the JSON log format, the field now contains the following string (note the capital `W`):
```
Waiting for connections
```

The regex should probably be changed to
```
Wait.forLogMessage("(?i).*waiting for connections", 1)
```
in order to support both versions. Can you try this out @remal? If it works, feel free to submit a PR to fix this use.

@vcvitaly
> I see that many tests are using static tags. Do you think tests should be ran against the 'latest' tag?

I don't think this is a good idea since we have no control over what happens with the `latest` images. The only reasonable thing Testcontainers can guarantee is support for certain fixed image versions that comply with our implicit image expectations and constraints.

issue.title: Add support for MongoDB 4.4

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

issue.body:
Makes `LogMessageWaitStrategy` in `MongoDBContainer` compatible with MongoDB 4.4 images without breaking backwards compatibility (regex changed to `(?i).*waiting for connections.*`).

It is a bit unfortunate that this uses a full integration test for checking something trivial (working regex), so maybe there is a better approach using a mock/stub? Do we have other tests where we solve this on a unit test level?

Fixes #3077

body:
With 4.4.1 this worked for me:
`waitingFor(
                        Wait.forLogMessage(".*Waiting for connections*.*", 1)
                )`

I generally use HostPortWaitStrategy which does not rely on the internals of the image in use.
For example;
`new MongoDBContainer(mongoVersion)
    .waitingFor(Wait.forListeningPort().withStartupTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30)));`

With this, you don't have to keep changing your regex every time mongodb decides to change their log message. 

I would love to know if there is any practical difference between LogMessageWaitStrategy vs HostPortWaitStrategy (in the context of MongoDBContainer).

issue.title: Put memory limits on test docker containers
issue.body:
## What does this PR do?

In attempt to reduce test flakyness, we should constraint docker containers available memory.
The values are arbitrary, and should be low enough to always fit our test infrastructure and development machines.

- When the limit is set too low, the container startup fails with `Container crashed with out-of-memory (OOMKilled)` message.
- When the limit is not set, the container might use the host system memory as "available memory", which is the case by default when running elasticsearch image that starts with close to 16gb heap on a 32gb system, even if less than 16gb is actually available when starting it.
- Good heuristic when running tests: total system memory usage should stay more or less flat and not jump from ~50% to 99% usage when running the `*IT` tests through `mvn verify`.

-----
Also attempts to minimize `Container startup failed` failures which seem related to a docker bug that is making most containers relying on log parsing to detect proper startup to fail.
- https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/41820
- related testcontainers issue https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/issues/3613

Update: assertion on issues above have been removed, as it seems the outcome is still random and might still work as expected.
We work-around those for now by using an older CI image `debian-9`, this constraint could be removed once we have docker 20.10.6 available.

Update on Update: the `debian-9` tag has been removed, hopefully making it ready for when the related infra change is available, that allows to merge to master and already provide extra reliability.
